candidates.name: seeded-determinism-and-replay
candidates.description: Apply the single 32-bit seeded PRNG, its serialized state and the fixed consumption order for shuffles, reward offers, enemy plans and round seeds so seeded runs, saves and browser journeys replay identically, while battle-log dialogue uses a separate pure hash that never touches the engine PRNG.
candidates.reason: The battle log adds a second determinism path: LOG-NF-01 requires dialogue selection from a local hash of seed, ordinal and trigger, and LOG-FR-03 forbids reading or advancing the engine PRNG. The existing package covers engine randomness but needs additive guidance on keeping presentation deterministic without consuming the shared sequence.

candidates.name: versioned-local-persistence
candidates.description: Implement the three versioned Fieldbound localStorage keys with validate-before-use, discard-only-the-affected-key, injectable storage adapters and in-memory fallback, including additive optional fields inside an existing key without a schema-version bump.
candidates.reason: LOG-FR-06 adds an optional battleLog array inside fieldbound.run.v1, with no new key and no schema bump. The package covers key-level validation but needs the narrower additive-field rule: a malformed log drops only the log while the run and battle still resume.

candidates.name: portrait-first-board-and-accessibility
candidates.description: Build and verify the 375px-to-1080px board layout, 44px targets, glyph-plus-label element cues, focus return, polite live announcements, non-live history regions and the reduced-motion contract shared by the shell, the battle log and the release checks.
candidates.reason: LOG-FR-04 and LOG-FR-07 add a labelled log region, a 44px drawer toggle, Escape focus return, a 1024px column and an explicit ban on a second aria-live area. The existing package encodes board and live-region rules but not the log surface's no-double-announcement and drawer focus contract.

candidates.name: placeholder-asset-manifest
candidates.description: Generate deterministic SVG placeholders, publish the 41-entry asset manifest with spec metadata, resolve files through a base-URL-aware loader and keep the documented swap contract intact.
candidates.reason: Battle Log & Dynamic Dialogue adds no card, enemy, field or manifest entry and changes no asset path, so the existing package satisfies the feature unchanged.

candidates.name: static-build-origin-audit
candidates.description: Produce and audit the GitHub Pages subpath build with build-only CSP injection, zero cross-origin requests after load, a 307200-byte gzip budget and committed CI and Pages workflows.
candidates.reason: The feature adds no dependency, no origin, no build step and no CSP change. The existing audit package still governs the build, origin and budget proof used by LOG-08.

candidates.name: battle-log-and-deterministic-dialogue
candidates.description: Implement and verify the bounded battle log: one entry per settled transition, 80-entry truncation that preserves ordinals, public-only duel entries, factual prose plus one locally hashed dialogue line, non-live presentation, and additive solo save and resume.
candidates.reason: LOG-01 through LOG-08 repeat a fragile cross-cutting contract across seven owners: entry derivation from state deltas, ordinal-preserving truncation, a dialogue hash that must not consume the engine PRNG, duel public-only redaction, a non-live accessibility surface and an additive save field. No existing package covers this combination, and applying it from memory risks a second live region, a hand leak in duel or a lost Continue Run.

candidates.name: balance-tuning
candidates.description: Tune card, health, heal and enemy numbers from self-play and playtest evidence.
candidates.reason: VIS-CON-07 freezes every number for v1 and section 13 defers tuning to a documented follow-up, so encoding a tuning process now would contradict the current scope.

candidates.name: human-release-review
candidates.description: Perform the human release and battle-log reviews of both journeys and record readability, privacy, dialogue tone and runtime observations.
candidates.reason: REL-HR-1 and LOG-HR-1 are human-review tasks with no model owner; packaging them as a skill would invite an agent to fabricate the sign-off or readability judgement that the tasks exist to keep human.
